cleanIntro: The Condor is a break-action over/under and there is no field strip in the semi-auto sense: it comes apart into barrels, forearm and stock/frame and that is the end of what Stoeger publishes. This book is specifically the SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR model -- it says nothing about ejector or double-trigger Condors, and never names them. The work is bores, the standing breech, the frame's bearing surfaces and the two pivot pins the barrels hinge on; the choke tubes want checking every 50 shots and cleaning every 100.

steps.title: Break the action and let the extractor lift both chambers
steps.action: Rotate the top lock lever to the right and swing the barrels down. On this extractor-model Condor the shells are lifted proud of the chambers rather than thrown clear, so they come out in your fingers -- which means an unfired shell can sit back down if you close the gun again without taking it. Lift both out and look through both chambers before going further.
steps.caution: Opening the gun sets the safety to "S" automatically on the automatic-safety version.
steps.quote: TO UNLOAD — Rotate top lock lever to right and open action. Shells will be automatically extracted from gun and may be removed by hand, or ejected (if the case).
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / OVER AND UNDER SHOTGUN / CONDOR / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — TO UNLOAD, p.8

steps.title: This book is the CONDOR single trigger extractor model
steps.action: Check which Condor is in your hands before you follow anything here. The document names itself as the single-trigger, over/under, extractor model on its cover and again over the parts diagram, and it never mentions an ejector version or a double-trigger version anywhere. If your gun throws empties clear of the breech, or has two triggers, this is not its book.
steps.prose: The whole parts diagram is drawn for that one configuration.
steps.quote: CONDOR - SINGLE TRIGGER OVER/UNDER EXTRACTOR MODEL
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / OVER AND UNDER SHOTGUN / CONDOR / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — Parts diagram caption, p.2

steps.title: Shell size is what the barrel says, not what fits
steps.action: Read the gauge and chamber marking on the barrel and load nothing else. A shorter shell will chamber in a longer chamber and a 12 gauge gun will happily swallow a 20 gauge round down the bore, where it lodges and leaves room for a 12 behind it. Stoeger states the rule flatly for this gun, and on a break-action there is no feed mechanism to reject a wrong shell for you.
steps.quote: Special care should be taken to insure that gun is not loaded with any size other than marked on gun barrel.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / OVER AND UNDER SHOTGUN / CONDOR / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — p.10
steps.warn: DO NOT SHOOT STEEL SHOT THROUGH A FULL CHOKED BARREL

steps.title: Forearm off
steps.action: With the action open, press the forearm latch forward and push the front of the forearm down and away from the barrels. It releases as a unit and the barrels are then free to come off the frame. Take it right off before touching the barrels -- trying to lift the barrels with the forearm still latched loads the forearm iron against the frame radius.
steps.quote: TO REMOVE FOREARM ASSEMBLY — Press forearm latch forward. Push front of forearm assembly downward.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / OVER AND UNDER SHOTGUN / CONDOR / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — TO REMOVE FOREARM ASSEMBLY, p.8

steps.title: Barrels off the pivot pins
steps.action: With the forearm off and the action open, move the barrel assembly down slightly to disengage the two circular cuts on its underside from the pivot pins in the frame, then lift it upward and away. It is a short, deliberate motion -- the barrels do not slide off, they unhook. Support their weight as they come free rather than letting the muzzles swing down onto the bench.
steps.quote: TO REMOVE BARREL ASSEMBLY — Remove forearm assembly. Open action. Move barrel assembly downward slightly to disengage from pivot pins. Lift upward and remove from frame.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / OVER AND UNDER SHOTGUN / CONDOR / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — TO REMOVE BARREL ASSEMBLY, p.8

steps.title: Bores, breech faces and the frame's bearing surfaces
steps.action: Run both bores from the breech with a rod and lightly oiled patches, using nitro solvent and a brush if they are leaded or plastic-fouled, then wipe out and re-oil very lightly. Clean the top surfaces of the frame carefully: residue collecting there is what stops a Condor closing fully, and a gun that will not close all the way will not fire. Wipe every steel surface after handling -- a fingerprint's worth of moisture is enough to start rust on a blued break-action.
steps.prose: Grease, not oil, on the wear points: the frame's front radius where the forearm iron bears, the pivot pins, and the inside frame walls the barrel lumps touch.
steps.caution: In sub-freezing weather remove excess oil and use dry graphite or another non-congealing lubricant.
steps.quote: CLEANING AND CARE — Open action. Clean barrel bores with cleaning rod and soft, lightly oiled cloths. If necessary, scrub bores with nitro solvent. Wipe clean and re-oil very lightly.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / OVER AND UNDER SHOTGUN / CONDOR / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — CLEANING AND CARE, p.8

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrels, forearm and stock/frame are the three pieces this Condor separates into, and that is deliberately the end of it -- Stoeger does not recommend going further unless a part actually needs repair or replacement. Everything that fouls in normal shooting is reachable now. Deep Clean covers the forearm iron, which does come off for cleaning, and the choke tube schedule.
steps.prose: Anything past those is a gunsmith's job on this gun, by the manual's own instruction.
steps.quote: Any disassembly of the over and under shotgun described in the Gun Owner’s Manual in not recommended unless necessary for repair or replacement of worm or damaged parts. Select a qualified gunsmith or return gun to store.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / OVER AND UNDER SHOTGUN / CONDOR / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — p.9

deepSteps.title: Forearm iron out of the wood
deepSteps.action: With the forearm assembly off the gun, unscrew the front forearm screw and the rear forearm screw and pull the iron out of the wood, then slide the forearm iron assembly clear. Keep the two screws separate -- they are different and the wood is drilled for each in its own place. This is the one sub-assembly the Condor's manual does open, and only when the iron itself needs cleaning.
deepSteps.quote: TO REMOVE FOREARM IRON ASSEMBLY — Remove forearm assembly. Unscrew front forearm screw and rear forearm screw. Pull iron from forearm. Slide forearm iron assembly from forearm. Assemble in reverse.
deepSteps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / OVER AND UNDER SHOTGUN / CONDOR / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — TO REMOVE FOREARM IRON ASSEMBLY, p.8

deepSteps.title: Wash the iron in solvent, dry, re-oil sparingly
deepSteps.action: Wash the forearm iron assembly in solvent, dry it thoroughly and re-oil it sparingly before it goes back into the wood. Sparingly is the operative word: oil that soaks into the forearm wood softens the inletting around the iron over time, and the cocking lever this assembly carries needs a film, not a bath.
deepSteps.prose: Grease the matching radius on the front of the frame while both halves are apart.
deepSteps.quote: Should cleaning of parts of forearm iron assembly be required, remove assembly from forearm. Wash assembly in solvent, dry and re-oil sparingly.
deepSteps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / OVER AND UNDER SHOTGUN / CONDOR / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — CLEANING AND CARE, p.8

deepSteps.title: Choke tubes -- check at 50 shots, clean at 100
deepSteps.action: Take the screw-in chokes out with the choke tube wrench every hundred shots and clean them inside and out with lubricating oil and a piece of flannel, then press each firmly to the end of its seat on the way back in. Between cleanings, verify every fifty shots that the tubes are still tight. A choke backing out under recoil in an over/under barrel is how the tube gets swaged and the barrel threads with it.
deepSteps.prose: Never change a choke tube on a loaded gun, and never fire steel shot through a full choke in this Condor.
deepSteps.caution: Each time after 50 shots, verify if the SCREW-IN CHOKE is tightly set.
deepSteps.quote: Periodically (each time after 100 shots) remove the SCREW-IN CHOKE and clean internally a and externally using lubricant oil and a piece of flannel cloth.
deepSteps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / OVER AND UNDER SHOTGUN / CONDOR / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — SHOTGUNS - screw-in choke instructions, p.17

deepSteps.title: If the stock has been off, the stock bolt has a ceiling
deepSteps.action: Should the stock ever have been removed, torque the stock bolt back to no more than 5 ft-lbs. This is a real limit and not a guideline: overtightening the stock bolt on a Condor distorts the frame tail and can stop the gun functioning correctly, and a torque wrench is the only honest way to hit a number that low.
deepSteps.prose: Stoeger asks for special care in reassembling this joint for exactly that reason.
deepSteps.quote: The stock bolt should be tightened, to torque not exceeding 5 ft. lbs. Overtightening of stock bolt may adversely affect proper functioning of gun.
deepSteps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / OVER AND UNDER SHOTGUN / CONDOR / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — TO REASSEMBLE STOCK, p.8

cleaning.name: BORES & CHOKES
tasks: Clean both bores from the breech with a rod and lightly oiled cloths; nitro solvent and a brush if fouled
Wipe clean and re-oil very lightly
Verify choke tightness every 50 shots; remove and clean the tubes every 100
Never change a choke on a loaded gun; no steel shot through a full choke

cleaning.name: FRAME & LOCKUP
tasks: Clean the top surfaces of the frame -- residue there prevents the action closing fully
Keep the polished breech faces clean and lightly oiled
Grease the frame's front radius where the forearm iron bears
Grease the pivot pins and the inside frame walls that contact the barrel assembly

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & STORAGE
tasks: Oil-wipe every steel part after handling -- invisible moisture prints cause rust
After wet weather, dry and oil-wipe the steel; expect condensation on abrupt temperature changes
In sub-freezing weather remove excess oil and use dry graphite or a non-congealing lubricant

reassembly: Rotate the top lock lever right to hold the top lock open, then fit the two small circular cuts on the underside of the barrel assembly onto the frame's pivot pins.
Hold that engagement and rotate the barrels upward until the action closes and the top lock latches.
Offer the forearm assembly to the bottom barrel at a slight angle, match the radius on the forearm iron to the radius on the front of the frame, and press upward until it latches.
Close by holding the forearm in one hand and raising the stock with the other until it locks -- never force the barrels open or shut.
A new gun's top lever may not return to dead centre; that is deliberate take-up for wear, not a fault.
fncheck: Close the gun and check the top lever is firm in position 2 -- if it is not, the locking lugs stay exposed and will damage the extractor on the next closing, which is the specific failure this gun's manual calls out. Open and close the action a few times to confirm the barrels and forearm are correctly assembled and the lever snaps home each time. Confirm the safety moves to "S" as the action opens on the automatic-safety version, and that the action closes fully with no gritty resistance from residue on the frame's top surfaces.
